components.description: Eight dinner ideas only in Tokyo/Kyoto/Osaka reuse incumbent city/category pills and an 18px accent-colored spontaneous-only checkbox. This native Zauo specimen exposes reservation advice before expansion and embeds the actual original fishing scene; HIRAKUZA adds the same component with a dedicated Sumo scene and a direct day-alternative deep link. In the application, spontaneous filtering requires walkIn === true; the honest empty state resets category/spontaneous filtering while retaining the city. The two-column 16px-gap list stacks at 760px.
components.html:
Zauo Shinjuku · Das Essen selbst angelnTokyo · Erlebnis-EssenReservierung empfohlen

Das macht den Abend besonders

Ihr sitzt zwischen nachgebauten Fischerbooten und könnt euren Speisefisch selbst angeln. Die Küche bereitet den Fang nach Wunsch zu – ein echtes gemeinsames Erlebnis statt eines steifen Menüs.

Spontan oder reservieren?

Tischreservierung wird angeboten. Unsere Empfehlung: vorher reservieren, besonders für die Bootsplätze. Ein freier Tisch ohne Buchung ist nicht bestätigt.

Filiale, Kinderangebot & Reservierung

components.description: Five chronological native proposal rows show annual/programme-unconfirmed status before opening, with original flower/float/park-show scenes and family crowd/heat/exit guidance. This Iriya specimen uses the shipped flower geometry and 64×44px thumbnail; expanded image/copy columns stack at 760px. Day shortcuts open and focus the matching summary. A separate disclosure explains why Sumida/Tenjin fireworks are outside the stays; none of the current proposals claims a confirmed 2027 programme.
components.html:
7. Juli · TokyoIriya Asagao-matsuri · Prunkwinden-MarktJahrestermin · Programm 2027 noch prüfen

Termin & Verlässlichkeit

Traditionell 6.–8. Juli; der 7. ist unser Vorschlag zum Ueno-Tag. Die Veranstalterseite bestätigt bisher keine Ausgabe 2027.

Mit den Kids

Nur eine kurze Runde wählen, Getränke mitnehmen und bei Gedränge abkürzen. Prunkwinden blühen vor allem morgens; ein später Besuch ist eher Markt- als Blütenschau. Kein ruhiger, leerer Markt zugesagt.

Offizielles Programm prüfen

components.html:
1
Takeshita Street · Harajuku

Shopping & Streetfood

Unser Genuss-Tipp: AFURI Harajuku · Yuzu-Shio-Ramen

Klare Brühe mit frischem Yuzu-Zitrusaroma statt einer schweren, cremigen Ramen-Suppe. Die Harajuku-Filiale passt direkt in euren Viertelbummel.

Die Filiale ist laut Betreiber bargeldlos. Ein kleiner Ramenladen, keine garantiert lange Familien-Sitzpause.

narrative.overview:
“Playful, but clean” is expressed through rounded display lettering, festival red, blue and amber, and original outlined SVG scenery. Fuji, the train, torii, onigiri and suitcase belong to the same flat-vector world. The reference is a Japanese summer festival with a light rhythm-arcade influence, not copied game characters, logos or artwork.

The working interface is deliberately quieter than its illustration while carrying the same rhythm language. Neutral surfaces, thin dividers, clear labels and compact disclosures make practical detail readable; destination-colored day rings, four equal route tones, drum-like badges, beat-dot tracks, ticket edges and short four-color bars keep the planner from feeling like a spreadsheet. Controls and structure teach the interaction without tutorial prose.

Location detail pairs compact, numbered thumbnails with larger photo postcards on expansion. Licensed archive photographs show real places; clearly labeled original scenes cover missing or seasonally misleading imagery and the family dinner/festival options. This extends the incumbent festival world without changing the hero or introducing another visual system.
keyCharacteristics: Original outlined SVG festival geometry and locally hosted rounded lettering.
Festival red, blue and amber above quiet, theme-aware neutrals.
Four equally structured route tones with drum badges, beat tracks and ticket-like activity blocks.
A visible-only animated festival hero plus short state and navigation motion throughout the planner.
One selected day, labeled task tabs and closed-by-default detail.
Credited archive photos and explicit illustration labels, with booking/date status visible before expansion.
One-lane mobile routes switched only by visible buttons, plus dedicated day and lane-item detail screens.
A dedicated Home destination owns the banner and station strip; a compact animated mobile sitemap replaces the horizontal menu.
Measured desktop/tablet navigation overflow moves into a More disclosure rather than a horizontal scrollbar.
An original Shinkansen destination selector with landmark windows and bounded, reduced-motion-aware landscape parallax.
Controls remain self-explanatory without tutorial or hand-holding copy.

rules.name: The Festival Roles Rule
rules.body: Component colors reference the existing `--cp-*` variables; festival red, blue and amber keep their built roles instead of becoming a second hard-coded palette.

rules.name: The Display/Detail Rule
rules.body: Lilita One gives headings and meaningful route/date numerals their character; the local UI stack carries controls and long practical copy.

rules.name: The Flat Planner Rule
rules.body: Separate planning surfaces with the existing borders and theme-aware fills; do not infer ambient, glass or hard-offset card elevation from unused theme variables or screenshot tiles.

dos: **Do** use the exact existing `--cp-*` variables and their light/dark assignments for every component color.
**Do** pair locally hosted Lilita One headings with the recorded local UI body stack.
**Do** keep the selected-day overview compact, with complete route lanes, explicit travel and selected place/food detail behind the two labeled day-local tabs.
**Do** repeat the original rhythm signature through destination day rings, equal route tones, drum badges, beat dots, ticket edges and short four-color bars.
**Do** reserve looping motion for the visible hero scene; use short motion elsewhere to explain selection, disclosure and navigation state, with complete Reduce Motion support.
**Do** use original, consistent SVG icons and scenery; preserve visible focus, meaningful state and reduced-motion behavior.
**Do** let controls, grouping and status labels explain interaction; retain factual travel, booking, safety, child and uncertainty guidance.
**Do** credit local archive photos with author, source, license and crop wording; explicitly label original illustrations and explain image failures without hiding independent links.
**Do** expose booking requirements and unconfirmed festival dates before expansion, keeping family evening choices optional.
**Do** keep map consent, attribution, recoverable loading states and independent place links visible where relevant.
donts: **Don't** copy game or film characters, logos, artwork or music into authored UI assets to strengthen the festival reference.
**Don't** replace the primary display face with an installed system display font or use emoji/glyphs as the icon system.
**Don't** add invented kickers, hard-offset card shadows or a synthetic color palette as inherited house style.
**Don't** restore tutorial prose that explains how to click, swipe, expand, read route lanes or use the day map.
**Don't** restore removed budget, template/source-reference, print or footer UI on the authority of dormant selectors or stale notes.
**Don't** treat automated map fixture tiles, unused theme effects or tiny one-off artwork lettering as reusable design tokens.
**Don't** present an illustration as a location photograph, a walk-in policy as guaranteed availability or an annual festival rule as a confirmed 2027 programme.
